$comment: Modules an extracted application also holds, byte for byte.
Each was duplicated rather than moved, and each for a reason recorded in the
extraction that did it:
polyline / activity-meta / track / tile-math — Main and Health both use
these route geometry primitives. If the copies diverge, distance and
activity calculations can silently disagree.
file-store/storage — the boundary linter classifies it PLATFORM and
thirteen non-Drive modules import it, including the public hero video.
Both copies point at one WORKFLOW_FILES_ROOT.
file-shares / file-serving — the share capability is minted by one process
and may be resolved by the other. Divergence is a valid link rejected.
intel/source-policy — the pure half of the folder policy; its DB-aware half
stayed here.
None of these drifting breaks a build or fails a test. That is exactly why
the hashes are recorded. Change one, change it in the peer repo too, then:
node scripts/record-shared-modules.mjs
apple-health-scale — the x100 that apple_health_metrics.value is stored in.
The ingest that multiplies now lives in SR-Health; the two readers that
divide are here, and both are public: the homepage's step count and the
vitals poll's pulse. A factor that disagreed across the boundary would not
fail a build or log anything, it would just be wrong by a hundred — which
this repo has already shipped once.
health-context-contract — the shape SR-Health's /api/health/context returns
and the chat context panel renders. Types only, so both repos hold it byte
for byte. Redeclaring it instead is how a field starts arriving undefined
with nothing red anywhere.
file-index/* — this is a MAIN module that Drive borrowed, not the reverse.
/dav, deepdive/to-drive, intel/mail-admit, knowledge/search, the file-search
workflow node, the file_* agent tools, jkai/media/preanalyse and
/api/jkai/attachments all need it here. If the copies diverge, the same file
indexed by one application is found differently by the other.
store.ts is deliberately NOT here: Drive's copy hands Intelligence a row
instead of importing its engine, which is the whole point of that boundary.
health-sync/* — the Strava and WHOOP INGEST lane, which is ours and stays.
It moved out of $lib/health so that tree can be deleted wholesale once the
dashboard half is gone. SR-Health holds the same five, because /api/health/
sync and the two OAuth callbacks are routed to it, so BOTH applications
refresh the same tokens and write the same tables.
Concurrency is already handled — readOrRefreshToken takes
pg_advisory_xact_lock and re-reads inside the transaction. Divergence is
not: `refreshToken: newTokens.refresh_token || token.refreshToken` is
WHOOP's rotation, and if one repo changes that line both connectors die
with nothing red anywhere.
scheduler.ts is NOT here. It is ours alone — the timer must run exactly
once — and SR-Health's copy is dead code being deleted rather than guarded.
planner-sports — the sports SR-Health's planner accepts and the cap ORS puts
on a round trip. The route_plan tool builds its `sport` enum and its
distance wording from them when the tool registry LOADS, which cannot wait
on another process. Drift offers the model a sport Health rejects, and a
400 inside a tool call reads to a model as a broken route service rather
than a bad argument.
health-signals-contract — the derived health figures and the segment
taxonomy the daydream sampler records each day. Both endpoints exist only
for this caller and annotate their responses with these types, so a rename
there fails the check there. The sampler indexes the field names to build
its readings; a rename is a signal that silently stops being recorded.
list.ts was registered here by mistake and removed when the drive tree was
deleted: it is the one file-index module that is Drive-only, so there is no
copy on this side to keep in step.
THE PLATFORM SET — money, credentials, permissions.
Every extracted application builds standalone, so it carries its own copy
of the platform layer. A sweep on 2026-09-13 found 318 byte-identical
files across the three repositories and nine registered. Registering all
318 would be wrong: most are the strangler fig, and a guard that fires on
every ordinary change gets routed around.
These fifteen are the ones where divergence is SILENT AND EXPENSIVE, and
they were chosen on evidence rather than taste — each changed between 0
and 4 times in ninety days, so the guard is cheap insurance rather than
noise.
llm/* — pricing, the usage log, the usage meter, key selection and the
client itself. All three applications make LLM calls and write to the
same spend tables. Diverge and the cost of a call depends on which
application made it, and nothing says so.
secrets/crypto — a credential encrypted by one process and unreadable by
another.
datastore/permissions + audit — who may read what, in a datastore all
three share. A permission decision that differs by application is a
security bug that no test anywhere would catch.
server/access, access-util, owner, config/owner — the owner check.
server/rate-limit, ssrf-guard — a guard that is stricter in one
application than another is a guard with a door in it.
health-sync/strava.ts left both repositories on 2026-09-13. The INTEGRATION
was removed, not the data: strava_activities keeps its 671 rows and stays
declared (operations.json lists it as required), and types.ts still
describes them, so it is deliberately unchanged.
The four webdav/* modules left both repositories on 2026-09-13 with the
WebDAV mount itself. webdav_credentials keeps its declaration — the two
rows were created and last used on 9 May, a connection test and nothing
since — because an undeclared table is a DROPPED table.
THE NAV KIT — the one bar, held in four repositories.
site-nav.ts is the manifest that decides a path's section, its sub-nav, its
parent and whether it wears the bar at all; SiteHeader.svelte renders it;
page-path.ts reads the current path without touching $app/state.
These are registered because of what happened on 2026-09-18, not on principle.
Policy Analysis moved under /projects and /live was retired. This repository's
copy followed; the three vendored copies did not, so /drive and nine /health
pages went on offering a cell to a URL that had moved and one to a page with no
owner in SR-Infra's registry. Nothing failed. deploy/kit.json guards gateway/
and scripts/ only, so a vendored file under src/ had no guard of any kind.
The failure is quiet by construction: a stale nav still compiles, still renders
and still passes every test in the repository that holds it. It is only wrong
against THIS repository, which is why the check belongs here.
SR-Policy-Analysis holds page-path.ts byte for byte and is named for it. Its
site-nav.ts and SiteHeader.svelte are deliberately NOT registered: that copy
carries real /projects/broads-pilot and /broads/speed chrome exclusions this
repository does not have, and puts data-sveltekit-reload on the whole header
because every cell in that application leaves it. A guard that fires on a
difference that is meant to be there gets routed around.
SR-JKAI is NOT named. It holds all three, but only on move/routes-wip — its
master has no src/lib/nav at all. A peer is somewhere a change can GO, and an
unmerged branch is not that. When that branch lands, re-sync the three files
against this repository and add the peer here.
